sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time (UTC): 2026-11-10 01:43 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-10 through 2026-11-10. Ranking basis: GitHub Trending daily star gains, descending; current total stars corroborated via GitHub REST API.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Today's strongest signal is a surge in practical AI-agent infrastructure—from agent skills and browser control to multi-agent desktop apps—alongside a large spike for the established Sherlock OSINT utility. Meta's agent-ready design system and a privacy-oriented WiFi sensing project broaden the day's themes beyond agent tooling.

sections.title: sherlock-project/sherlock
sections.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks; the current README says it covers 400+ networks.
sections.why_notable: Leads this snapshot by daily star gain, showing that a focused, mature OSINT utility can break through alongside AI launches.

sections.title: meta/astryx
sections.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready; the README describes a React 19+ and StyleX-based system with 150+ accessible components.
sections.why_notable: Its strong second-place daily gain puts design infrastructure built for both people and coding agents in the day's spotlight.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository README labels the project as currently in beta.

sections.title: milind-soni/OpenMausBot
sections.description: An open-source desktop alternative for chatting with a team of AI bots; the README describes Claude or Codex agents running locally behind bots with distinct personalities and connected apps.
sections.why_notable: Its momentum reflects interest in agent teams packaged as an interactive, user-facing app.

sections.title: anthropics/skills
sections.description: Anthropic's public examples of reusable skills for Claude; each skill is a self-contained folder of instructions, scripts, and resources.
sections.why_notable: The repository is a high-visibility example of agents gaining repeatable task workflows through self-contained skills.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-browser
sections.description: A Rust CLI for browser automation driven by AI agents; the README describes accessibility-tree snapshots, element refs, and a persistent browser session.
sections.why_notable: Its inspect-act-verify shell loop is a concrete pattern for tool-using agents.

sections.title: google-deepmind/mujoco
sections.description: A general-purpose physics simulator for articulated structures interacting with their environment; maintained by Google DeepMind.
sections.why_notable: Represents robotics and embodied simulation, with a maintained C API and interactive visualization.

sections.title: anthropics/claude-quickstarts
sections.description: Deployable example applications built with the Claude API, including customer support, financial analysis, and computer-use demos.
sections.why_notable: Its range of examples connects model capabilities to practical app workflows.

sections.title: ZhuLinsen/daily_stock_analysis
sections.description: An LLM-powered, multi-market stock-analysis dashboard combining market data, real-time news, and scheduled notifications.
sections.why_notable: It is a prominent domain-specific AI application combining market data, news, analysis, and delivery integrations.

sections.title: garrytan/gbrain
sections.description: A self-hostable memory layer designed to make explicit, sourced facts available across AI agents, with correction and withdrawal support.
sections.why_notable: It adds persistent, user-controlled context to the agent-infrastructure cluster.

sections.title: ruvnet/RuView
sections.description: A WiFi-signal sensing project for spatial presence and vital-sign estimation without camera video.
sections.why_notable: It is a distinctive privacy-oriented sensing theme, connecting commodity wireless signals with spatial and health-related inference.

sections.title: homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp
sections.description: An MCP server for configuring and automating Home Assistant with AI assistants.
sections.why_notable: It is a concrete example of agents acting on a real home-automation environment rather than only generating text.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflows and orchestration appear in anthropics/skills, anthropics/claude-quickstarts, OpenMausBot, and GBrain. Agent-to-tool integration appears in agent-browser and ha-mcp, while MuJoCo provides robotics simulation. Astryx brings an agent-ready React/StyleX design system; Sherlock leads the non-agent utility signal; RuView represents camera-free WiFi sensing; and daily_stock_analysis applies LLMs to multi-market research. Languages: Python 5/11, TypeScript 3/11, Rust 2/11, C++ 1/11.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The day's repo mix points to agents moving from model demos toward usable systems: reusable skills, browser and home-automation controls, shared memory, and desktop experiences. At the same time, Sherlock's lead and the presence of MuJoCo, RuView, and a finance-focused app show that momentum is not confined to agent frameworks; established utilities and specialized applications remain capable of attracting sharp attention.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content: Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily, captured 2026-11-10 01:43 UTC. Corroboration: GitHub REST repository endpoints for all 11 listed projects, including current star totals, descriptions, default branches, and branch-head commit SHAs; GitHub Search API queries for the five highest-momentum repositories confirmed identity, star totals, and push recency. Current README files were checked for the five narration-priority projects. Daily gains and ranking come from the matching Trending daily view; this is a one-day snapshot and not a claim about longer-term growth.
